newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico maquiladora employment rose 18.1 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Mexico maquiladora employment rose 18.1 pct in Dec.

text.p: Employment in Mexico's maquiladora, or in-bond industry, increased 18.1 percent in December compared with the same month the year before, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) said in a statement Thursday.
INEGI said the maquiladora industry employed an additional 17.3 percent in 1996 from the previous year.
The sector in December employed a total 803,060 people, the institute said.
Almost 82 percent of maquiladoras are concentrated in the states of Chihuahua, Baja California, Tamaulipas, Coahuila and Sonora.
Hours worked in December climbed 22.2 percent in December 1996 versus the year before, and rose 19.7 percent in 1996 from 1995.
The industry in 1996 generated about 48.88 billion current pesos in added value, divided into salaries and benefits, different operating expenses, profits and materials, INEGI said.

Electric materials and accessories accounted for 25.2 percent of added value, construction and transportation equipment assembly 23.1 percent, clothing assembly 11.8 percent, machinery and electronics assembly 11.3 percent, other manufacturing 10.6 percent and wood and metal products 6.7 percent.
